title: Japan's Osaka City says about 1.08 million email addresses leaked in administrative system breach via unauthorized access to contractor Arara
text:

The cause was that the operator to which the city outsources the system used an email delivery service provided by Arara, which suffered a cyberattack. On the same day, Osaka Prefecture disclosed that identity verification documents for 12 applicants and other individuals leaked in its food expense support program. Key Elements 
 Osaka City Arara Hideyuki Yokoyama Osaka Prefecture My Number Card premium gift certificate program administrative online system food expense support program for children and university students Osaka City said on the 13th that approximately 1.08 million email addresses related to users of its administrative online system had leaked externally. The cause was that the operator contracted to run the system used a service from email delivery company Arara, which had been hit by a cyberattack. Personal information such as names and My Number identifiers was not included, the city said.
 According to the city's digital administration office, the confirmed leak involved 1,078,713 addresses that received emails from the system between July 1 and October 31, including usage guidance, registration and password change procedures. The scope expanded significantly because the city sent a mass email in September informing users of improvements to the system's convenience.
 Separately, it was also found that Arara's service was used in this fiscal year's premium gift certificate program, and 48,537 email addresses of users and participating stores combined had leaked. The city said it has received no reports of secondary damage so far.
 Mayor Hideyuki Yokoyama appealed to residents on the 13th, saying, "Government offices will not ask for things like your ID, password or date of birth, so please do not enter such information if you receive a suspicious email."
 On the same day, Osaka Prefecture also announced that there had been unauthorized access to the system for its food expense support program for households raising children and young people, and that image data of identity verification documents for a total of 12 applicants and eligible individuals had leaked. The documents included My Number Cards, driver's licenses and health insurance cards, according to the prefecture. The program was implemented by the prefecture as an inflation relief measure and received about 1.4 million applications between March 26 and June 25 this year. The prefecture said it has not confirmed any misuse of the leaked data or leaks involving anyone other than the 12 people.
 In response to the incidents, Osaka City and Osaka Prefecture each plan to proceed with consideration of measures to prevent recurrence. As the digitalization of administrative services advances, the security management framework across the entire supply chain, including contractors, is once again being called into question.
